reading.body:
The itQ Data Center in Wrocław, Poland is an unverified OpenStreetMap record with no capacity figure, no confirmed operator, and no independent source beyond its own name.

The record carries a name that plainly signals IT and data-center services, a website address, and a location in one of Poland's larger technology and outsourcing hubs. That combination makes it a plausible genuine small facility rather than a mislabeled building. But plausibility is all the data supports. The capacity field is zero, the operator field is empty, and the research note states that no operator website, press coverage, or Polish business registration could be confirmed because the search quota ran out.

For AI infrastructure, the distinction between a plausible name and a verified facility is the whole question. Compute capacity is what matters, and this record contains none. A data center that cannot be tied to an operator, a power draw, or a registered business cannot be counted toward any regional capacity estimate, and treating it as though it could would inflate the picture.

What this does not tell the reader is whether itQ exists as a business, how large it is, or what it runs. It also says nothing about power supply, which is the constraint that governs whether any facility in this region can scale. The record is a lead awaiting confirmation, not a data point.
